title: Fintech has reshaped India’s financial system, taken banking to every citizen: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra- Moneycontrol.com
text:
My Alerts Go Ad-Free Follow us on: Speaking at the inauguration of the Global Fintech Fest, Malhotra said that fintech companies have acted as bridges to connect the vast population to formal credit systems in an affordable manner   September 08, 2026 / 19:57 IST             Fintech has fundamentally changed the architecture of India’s financial landscape and taken banking to the most rural areas of the country through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), Aadhaar-enabled ecosystems and the Jan Dhan ecosystem, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said on September 8. Speaking at the inauguration of the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai, Malhotra said fintech companies have acted as bridges connecting the vast population to formal credit systems in an affordable manner, while improving customer experience and efficiency in financial infrastructure. “Over the past decade, fintech has fundamentally reshaped the architecture of Indian finance. It has taken banking from the branch to the hand of every citizen,” Malhotra said. Technology has helped reduce account-opening and payment-settlement times, cut transaction costs, strengthen fraud detection through AI-driven analytics and enable real-time supervision, Malhotra said. Fintech has had a more tangible impact on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), where cash flow-based lending, account aggregators and the Unified Lending Interface are helping bridge India’s MSME credit gap by extending formal credit to small businesses, according to Malhotra. “The Reserve Bank has consistently viewed fintech as a valuable partner in building the financial system of the future. The regulatory sandbox, the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub and our structural and continued dialogues with startups, fintechs and other stakeholders all rest on the conviction that better policy emerges from continuous, open and constructive engagement,” Malhotra said. He further said that the central bank has encouraged self-regulation within the sector. The central bank has also remained open to new ideas and players while seeking to promote responsible innovation, he said.
